title: 07 — Station launch from approved upgrade ending
prompt:
Five-second photoreal single continuous fixed-wide shot, beginning EXACTLY from the supplied approved transformation-ending frame. Riley has just returned to this standing pose after her upgrade. Keep her precise position, scale, face, short brunette bob with subtle teal accents, viewer-right cheek cyberware, neck hardware, gold wrap mini-dress, black-and-gold boots, and mostly natural skin with narrow chrome/cyan inlays. No new transformation or costume change.

The train has ALREADY LEFT toward the distant SCREEN-LEFT vanishing point. The tracks behind Riley remain EMPTY throughout. Same wet station platform, morning light, architecture, signs and reflections as the start frame. The camera remains locked in place without reframing, zooming, tracking or cuts.

Immediate decisive takeoff: during the first0.35 seconds she flicks her gaze toward SCREEN LEFT, turns her shoulders and hips in that direction, and plants a boot with a compact athletic knee bend. No long pose, eye close-up, theatrical crouch, hovering or hesitation. By0.5 seconds she pushes HARD off the platform, launching diagonally toward SCREEN LEFT and AWAY from the camera along the safe platform path, parallel to the empty tracks. Show two or three clear connected running strides and rapidly increasing displacement. Her feet contact the ground naturally; she never crosses or jumps onto the rails. Hair and dress respond to the speed; maintain covered gold dress fabric over her back and hips.

By roughly1.8 seconds she has raced into the far-left distance, becoming small from actual travel rather than teleporting. Use a narrow brief cyan/magenta wake with restrained bloom, always behind her; keep her body and initial leg action readable. The wake fades, leaving the same empty platform for the remainder. The train must not reappear. No reverse direction, toward-camera run, extra people, duplicate Riley, stretched limbs, changed costume, fully robotic body, explosion or new obstacles.

Native sound: one tight boot plant, rapidly accelerating foot contacts and a short forceful air rush on launch, fading into quiet station ambience and a distant receding train. No speech, grunts, narration or music. Stylish confident speed with believable physical push-off.

model_guide.guide:
# Seedance family — bytedance-seedance-v1-pro, bytedance-seedance-v1.5-pro, bytedance-seedance-v2, bytedance-seedance-v2-fast, bytedance-seedance-v2.5, bytedance-seedance-v2.5-edit, bytedance-seedance-v2.5-extend, bytedance-seedance-v2-us, bytedance-seedance-v2.5-us, bytedance-seedance-v2.5-edit-us, bytedance-seedance-v2.5-extend-us

ByteDance's flagship video model. The first model supporting simultaneous quad-modal input (text, image, video, and audio). Strong motion realism, character consistency, and multi-shot storytelling.

## Inputs

- Text prompt
- Optional reference image. The model cites these as `@image1`, `@image2` — but do not type that yourself: place an `image_reference` part where the reference belongs and the backend renders the token there.
- Optional reference video
- Optional audio track (model choreographs video to sound, beat-matched)
- Parameters: resolution and duration vary by variant (see below)

## Variant notes

- **Seedance 2.0 / 2.0 Fast** — up to 4K (2.0) or 1080p (Fast); clips 4–15s.
- **Seedance 2.5** (`bytedance-seedance-v2.5`) — sharper realism; up to 1080p; clips up to 30s; much larger reference budget (upto 10 image, video, and audio refs). Prefer 2.5 over 2.0 unless the user names 2.0.
- **Seedance 2.5 Edit** (`bytedance-seedance-v2.5-edit`) — edit an existing clip by describing the change. Duration follows the source.
- **Seedance 2.5 Extend** (`bytedance-seedance-v2.5-extend`) — continue from the end of an existing clip. Prompt what happens next.
- **US-hosted variants** (`bytedance-seedance-v2-us`, `bytedance-seedance-v2.5-us`, `-edit-us`, `-extend-us`) — the same models served from US infrastructure, offered where the standard ids are not available; same resolutions as their counterparts, and 2.0 US takes no seed. Prompt them exactly like their counterparts.
- Fast and Pro / 2.5 share prompting style. Longer variants tolerate longer prompts.

## Prompt structure

```
[shot] + [subject] + [action] + [environment / lighting] + [style]
```

## Key strengths

- **Handles physical interactions** (pouring, splashing, hand-object contact) better than most models. Describe them concretely.
- **Good at weather and atmospheric effects.**
- **Audio-to-video** — upload an audio track and the model choreographs video to the sound with beat-matched cuts and lip sync.
- **Negative prompts work** — phrases like "no distortion, no stretching," "no grain, no shadows" are effective.
- **Seedream + Seedance pipeline** — generate reference images with Seedream, then use as visual references for maximum control.

## For image-to-video

- **Describe the motion, not the image.** "Camera slowly orbits around her" works far better than re-describing what she looks like.
- **Lock the character with consistency language** — add "maintain exact appearance from reference image" or "consistent character throughout, no deformation or drift."

## Rules

- **A wired audio reference needs `generate_audio` on.** With it off the render comes back silent and the track you connected is thrown away, so connecting audio turns it back on — never set it to false to keep a voiceover "clean".
- **Use one continuous action per clip.** Multi-beat narratives drift.
- **For start/end frame inputs**, write a prompt that bridges the two states ("from sealed package to fully revealed product"), not a static description.

## Example

> Wide tracking shot of a courier riding an electric scooter through a rainy Shanghai night market. Neon shopfronts reflect on wet pavement. Wisps of steam rise from food stalls as he weaves between pedestrians. Cinematic, slightly desaturated, shallow depth of field.

## What to avoid

- Re-describing the reference image in image-to-video prompts (wastes prompt budget).
- Abstract or heavily stylized prompts without specificity.

continuity_review.launch_direction: screen-left and away along platform, parallel to rails

assistant_visual_review.method: Twenty native samples every0.25 seconds plus nine context-join samples every0.125 seconds and full-frame decoding; approved source/diagnostic endpoints also inspected. Numeric audio review only, not continuous playback/listening.
observations: Starts from the approved standing Riley pose and same cleared station composition. Gold dress, bob, face/neck cyberware, human limbs with narrow chrome accents and dark/gold boots broadly retained.
Riley looks and turns screen left, then starts a visible running push-off around2.2–2.5 seconds.
She travels diagonally left and away along the platform, shrinking with distance; tracks stay empty and no train reset is visible.
Narrow cyan/magenta wake follows the run; camera/background remain broadly fixed.
Diagnostic-return-to-launch comparison has close composition/pose continuity around its one-second join in sampled frames.
limitations: Launch is much later than the requested0.5 seconds; wind-up occupies roughly the first two seconds. This is not yet an immediate takeoff in the existing1.25s slot.
She remains visible in the far distance through the ending; requested clear exit/empty-platform hold by1.8 seconds was not achieved.
Full-speed impact, foot contacts and exact likeness require playback judgment; sample images do not establish believable sprint cadence.
Native audio decoded and measured only; no independent listening or speech/music absence approval.
No final range selection, retiming or accepted-ad replacement. Continuity review preserves all native timing so the delay remains visible.
